title: lint: state-machine-no-initial-states should not judge update-only machines, where initialStates is inert
body:
repo:objectstack#1 · os-warren · session_01JQwxbXGvw43spR79ztEvWt

## What

PR #35244 (card #34776) adds the publish-time rule `state-machine-no-initial-states`. It refuses a `state_machine` validation with no `initialStates`. The engine applies `initialStates` only when the machine runs on insert. A machine declared with `events: ['update']` never runs on create, so the fix the finding asks for produces metadata the runtime ignores. That is the very trap class #34776 closes.

The #34776 dev measured this on PR #35244 (report on #34776, round 2). Three showcase machines are update-only: `showcase_account` `account_lifecycle`, `showcase_project` `project_health_progression` and `showcase_task` `task_status_flow`. To pass the rule, they now carry `initialStates` that state the entry state without enforcing it.

## Scope

- The rule judges only machines that run on insert, meaning their `events` include `insert` or default to it. Its hint stays as written.
- Remove the three declaration-only `initialStates` lists from the showcase, unless the showcase owner wants them as documentation.
- Add a negative pin for an update-only machine with no `initialStates`.
- Read whether `events` defaults to include insert in `packages/spec/src/data/validation.zod.ts` before writing the predicate.

Blocked until #35244 merges.

## Origin

Seat answer B on PR #35244: the rule ships as written, and this card carries the narrowing. #34776 claim amendment 6987471285, with the seat note that follows it.

Re-check: `git grep -n "state-machine-no-initial-states" origin/main -- packages/lint/src`
